text:
Alex: FYI seeing a large number of pod attach failures in apac-1 starting ~15m ago. GPU provisioning errors and slow controller reconciles. :rotating_light:
Jana: confirm, logs show BGP flap from our primary egress ISP in apac region. Packets to upstream are timing out, healthchecks failing.
Mike: impact: new Dedicated slot allocations failing, jobs stuck in Pending. Customers hitting elevated latency for hosted endpoints in apac-1.
Carla: any automatic fallback? I thought we had secondary peering.
SRE-Oncall: autoscaler is healthy but our egress NAT gateways rely on ISP-A. We have a secondary peer (ISP-B) but traffic isn't failing over due to route preference. Working on prep for manual re-route.
Alex: ok can we shift control-plane egress and data-plane traffic to ISP-B without full region drain? What's the blast radius?
Jana: route change will flip via FRR on border routers. Risk: short BGP reconvergence (~30-90s) and transient packet loss. No controller restart required.
Mike: ops playbook step: run `frrctl advertise-asn --peer ISP-B --region apac-1` then adjust MED.
Carla: Support wants a customer-facing status update and ETA. Can we give a realistic ETA?
SRE-Oncall: if we kick the route now, estimate 10-15m for re-route and then 60-90m for provisioning backlog to clear. So ETA ~1.5 hours.
SupportLead: I'll draft the status page — short, actionable, mention mitigation and ETA. Need link to workaround (route customers to us-east).
Alex: we should also open a prioritized support tag for impacted customers and offer fallback to cross-region traffic shift for critical workloads.
SupportLead: agreed. I'll create a ticket template and notify CSMs.
OpsBot: Deploy bot: observing partial route announcement from ISP-B in apac-1 (0:03).
Jana: starting manual route failover now. Running:```
# switch egress to ISP-B
frrctl update-route --region apac-1 --set-preference ISP-B --adjust-med 100
```
Mike: executing traffic-drain for apac heavy pools to reduce packet-loss impact: `reroute-pool --region apac-1 --to us-east1 --drain 45m`
Carla: status page draft (SupportLead please review):
"APAC (apac-1) — Degraded provisioning and elevated latency due to an upstream ISP egress outage. We are routing traffic to a secondary ISP and initiating traffic fallbacks to reduce customer impact. Estimated time to full recovery: ~90 minutes. Updates to follow."
SupportLead: published to status.redwood.ai/incidents/1855-apac-egress (short link) :white_check_mark:
SRE-Oncall: initial route change observable, BGP converged on some POPs. We're seeing provisioning success rate increase from 40% -> 70% in last 5m.
Alex: good. notify partners and SOC for compliance logs. Any customers requesting manual failover?
SupportLead: one enterprise (acme-corp) on a dedicated pool asked for immediate cross-region failover. I've queued a manual transfer and informed them of potential DB latency.
Jana: monitoring KV cache invalidation risk for cross-region; we should throttle concurrent failovers.
Mike: noted. throttling set to 2 concurrent pool moves. Command: `pool-move --concurrency 2`
Carla: support queue: TKT-7890 flagged high priority, assigned to SupportLead and Alex.
SRE-Oncall: continuing to monitor egress telemetry and provisioning backlog. Will update every 15m or on major milestone.
SupportLead: posting update on status page: "Route change in progress. Provisioning success improving. ETA ~60 minutes until all queued allocations are cleared."
Alex: :thumbsup: great work. Keep C-level succinct updates to product@ for any SLAs impacted.
OpsBot: Alert: route flaps decreased, packet-loss to ISP-A <1% (post-change).
Jana: final note — file RCA entry after stabilization (root cause: ISP-A hardware maintenance + misadvertised prep suffix).
